# Launch windows report

Computed by `scripts/generators/gen_launch_windows.py` (Global Commons spec § 5.3, § 5.2a) for 1900.01 to 2136.01. A window is the Hohmann optimum's calendar month and the months either side. Premiums are `exp(extra delta-v / 3.7 km/s) - 1` against the cycle's best window month, the extra delta-v averaged over 16 cycles spread across the span; the spread is the range of the individual cycles' premiums. Delta-v: departure from a 200 km parking orbit, capture into an orbit of eccentricity 0.9 at a tenth of a radius up at a planet, rendezvous at a small body. Nuclear thermal (NTP) premiums are the same extra delta-v at 9 km/s (Nuclear Thermal Propulsion, lunar colonization design § 9): `exp(extra delta-v / 9 km/s) - 1`, or `(1 + p)^(3.7 / 9) - 1` of the chemical premium p. A country with the technology pays them; transit is unchanged.

## The off-window rule on Mars

A full bar launches outside a window when goal × premium ÷ pace ≤ k × m (Standard k = 1, Ambitious 2; m = months to the next free window), in a 26-month cycle, goal 400, on chemical and on nuclear thermal (NTP) premiums:

| Pace | Standard launches | Ambitious launches | Standard, NTP | Ambitious, NTP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 a month | in the window only (3 in 26) | 2 months after (4 in 26) | 2 months after (4 in 26) | 2–3 months after (5 in 26) |
| 10 a month | 2 months after (4 in 26) | 2 months after (4 in 26) | 2–3 months after (5 in 26) | 2–10 months after (12 in 26) |
| 20 a month | 2 months after (4 in 26) | 2–3 months after (5 in 26) | 2–10 months after (12 in 26) | 2–12 months after; 2 months before (15 in 26) |
| 40 a month | 2–3 months after (5 in 26) | 2–10 months after (12 in 26) | 2–12 months after; 2 months before (15 in 26) | 2–13 months after; 2–12 months before (19 in 26) |

## Transit times

The months a colony fleet takes (solar colonization slices 2-3 design § 2), rounded, at least 1, except the Moon's 0: a fleet founds its world the month it leaves (lunar colonization design § 3.3). Chemical is the body's median Hohmann time, whatever the month. Fusion (Fusion Power): the shortest Lambert transfer within 30 km/s, from 0.05 to 2.6 times the Hohmann time. Fusion torch (Compact Fusion Reactors): a brachistochrone at 0.01 g, its delta-v capped at 400 km/s. Antimatter (Antimatter Production and an Antimatter Containment Facility): a brachistochrone at 0.03 g, its delta-v capped at 2,000 km/s. By months from the optimum, a departure on day 15 averaged over the premium's cycles; a better drive is never slower than the one before it.

| Body | Chemical | Fusion, in a window | Fusion torch, in a window | Antimatter, in a window |

| Mars | 9 | 2–3 | 1 | 1 |
| Ceres | 16 | 6–9 | 2 | 1 |

## Fleets' legs

The legs between the nine fleet locations (solar colonization slice 6 design § 1.2), in `common/script_values/sr_fleet_legs_generated.txt`. Each location is measured to one body: Mercury and Venus to Venus, Mars to Mars, the Asteroid Belt to Ceres, the Jupiter system to Jupiter, the Saturn system to Saturn, the Uranus system to Uranus, the Neptune system to Neptune, the Kuiper Belt to Kuiper. Departure from a planet's system starts in its loose capture orbit (eccentricity 0.9), from Earth in the 200 km parking orbit; arrival is that capture orbit, a rendezvous at a small body. Chemical's delta-v is the cheapest transfer of the departure's month; fusion's the shortest transfer within its budget; a torch's acceleration × time, at most its cap. Months are rounded, at least 1; a better drive is never slower.
